issues.legal_issue: Omitting property from an earlier partition suit does not bar a later claim to compensation where the property was acquired after that suit was filed.
material_facts: The earlier partition suit was filed in 1953.
The disputed property was purchased in the appellant’s name under a sale deed executed in 1961, so it could not have been included in the earlier suit when filed.
After the property was acquired and an award made, the respondents raised their claim to the compensation before the land acquisition authority, which referred the apportionment dispute to the court.
issues.conclusion: The omission did not bar the compensation claim, and Order II Rule 2 CPC did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Order II Rule 2 CPC did not apply because the property had not been purchased when the earlier partition suit was filed and therefore could not have been included in it. After acquisition and award, a claim concerning entitlement to the compensation could be pursued by raising an apportionment dispute before the land acquisition authority and through its reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

predicates.compensation_apportionment_reference: The proceeding concerns a dispute over apportionment of compensation referred to a court by an acquisition authority.
predicates.earlier_partition_filed_before_property_: A party filed a partition suit before the disputed property was acquired or purchased.
predicates.compensation_claim_raised_before_acquisi: The claimant raised the claim to a share of the compensation before the acquisition authority.

issues.definition: When a compensation-apportionment reference concerns property acquired after an earlier partition suit was filed, and the compensation claim was raised before the acquisition authority, the later claim is not barred by omission from that suit.

issues.legal_issue: Property acquired in the name of a family member is joint family property when the family had a sufficient nucleus and the purchase was made from joint family funds, unless the party asserting separate ownership establishes otherwise.
material_facts: The family manager purchased the property in the name of a minor family member, and the courts found that the consideration was paid from joint family funds.
The family had sufficient joint property that could have provided a nucleus for the purchase.
The appellant asserted that his maternal grandfather paid the consideration but failed to establish that assertion or that the property was purchased from the appellant’s separate funds.
The trial court and High Court both found the property to be joint family property after considering the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The property was joint family property, the respondents were each entitled to a share of the compensation, and there was no justification for disturbing the concurrent findings.
issues.legal_principle: There is no presumption that a joint family possesses joint property merely because the family is joint; the party alleging joint ownership must establish that the family had property whose income could have acquired the disputed property. If the family had joint property that could have formed a sufficient nucleus, the presumption arises that the disputed property was acquired with its aid, and the burden shifts to the party alleging self-acquisition to prove otherwise. The Court applied this principle in declining to interfere with the concurrent findings of the lower courts.

rule.if: compensation_apportionment_appeal and joint_family_had_sufficient_nucleus and purchase_made_from_joint_funds and claimant_failed_to_prove_separate_acquisition and concurrent_findings_supported_by_evidence

predicates.compensation_apportionment_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning ownership and apportionment of compensation awarded for acquired property.
predicates.joint_family_had_sufficient_nucleus: The family possessed joint property capable, in its nature and relative value, of providing a sufficient nucleus for the disputed purchase.
predicates.purchase_made_from_joint_funds: The family manager paid for the disputed property from joint family funds.
predicates.claimant_failed_to_prove_separate_acquis: The person asserting separate ownership did not establish that the purchase was made from separate funds.
predicates.concurrent_findings_supported_by_evidenc: The lower courts reached the same finding after considering evidence that supported their conclusion.

issues.definition: Where a compensation-apportionment appeal concerns property bought from joint family funds, the family had a sufficient nucleus, the asserted separate acquisition is unproved, and supported lower-court findings agree, the property is treated as joint family property and the concurrent finding is upheld.
